errors.text: The hypothesis introduces coherent FCC/B2 interfaces, nano-precipitates, and multiphase microstructures that are absent from the target single-crystal, single-phase equiatomic FeNiCrMn model.

The proposed strain-rate window of 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1 does not reconstruct the molecular-dynamics window of 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1, so its claimed rate-insensitivity boundary addresses a different physical regime.

The predicted cryogenic FCC-to-HCP transformation and strong strain-rate sensitivity conflict with the target result of Shockley-partial-mediated stacking faults, no bulk phase transformation, and negligible yield-rate sensitivity across the simulated range.
The cited coherent-interface studies do not establish that interface-assisted dislocation transfer causes yield strength to become strain-rate insensitive.
Evidence E5 uses a quinary nanowire at only one strain rate and therefore cannot support the claimed relationship between phase transformation and strain-rate sensitivity.
